newsitem.title: GERMANY: D.Telekom, Tele Danmark sign interconnect.
newsitem.headline: D.Telekom, Tele Danmark sign interconnect.

text.p: German telecommunications group Deutsche Telekom AG said on Tuesday it has signed an agreement with Tele Danmark that would allow the Danish phone company to access Telekom phone lines to reach customers in Germany.

The so-called interconnection deal follows a similar agreement signed last month with WorldCom, Inc. Deutsche Telekom said the two agreements are evidence of the company's willingness to grant competitors access to its networks.

"The contract signing with internationally experienced competitors is evidence that Deutsche Telekom is interested in quick conclusions and that it is possible to reach an agreement if both sides want to," said Telekom board member Herbert May.
"It should be possible to conclude further agreements soon," he added.
The interconnection agreement with Tele Danmark will be presented soon to German regulators for final approval. The WorldCom interconnection agreement is still pending final regulatory approval.
Because new competitors to former monopoly Deutsche Telekom do not have extensive networks in Germany they need to use the networks of Telekom to reach customers' homes or businesses.

Such interconnection agreements are common in competitive telecoms markets and the first such deals are now appearing in Germany as it prepares to open its telecoms market to full competition on January 1.

Domestic competitors Mannesmann Arcor and O.Tel.O, a joint venture of Veba AG and RWE AG, have filed complaints against Telekom with federal regulators, saying Telekom was not negotiating in good faith.
Telekom has dismissed the claims and says its domestic competitors lack the necessary experience to carry out such internconnection negotiations.
